summary: Verified Auto-Expire Appointments feature end-to-end. Backend 8/8 pytest pass: partial unique index `unique_nin_pending` exists with partialFilterExpression={status:'pending'}; startup auto-expire log confirmed ('Checking for past appointments to expire...' + 'Created partial unique index'); no pending past-dated appointments; booking rejected only when existing appointment is still pending; same NIN CAN rebook after status flipped to 'expired' or 'completed'; slot-availability counts only pending (expired appointment frees the slot). Frontend: Admin Dashboard shows gray 'Expired' badge, exposes an 'Expired' status filter button (data-testid=status-filter-expired), and renders 'No actions available' for expired rows. New booking happy path previously verified in iteration 5 remains green.

ui_bugs.issue: 'Pending' counter at the top uses `apt.status !== 'completed'` so it incorrectly includes 'expired' (and 'rejected') appointments. With an expired record present, Total=23 and Pending=23 while the actionable pending count is 22. Fix: `appointments.filter(a => a.status === 'pending').length`.

action_items: AdminDashboard.js L181: fix stats.pending to count only status === 'pending' (currently also counts expired/rejected).

Consider running the auto-expire job periodically (currently it runs only on FastAPI startup). Long-lived server processes will accumulate 'pending' records whose date has silently moved into the past until the next restart. A nightly/async task or on-request lazy-expire would be more robust.
critical_code_review_comments: Auto-expiration logic only fires inside the `@app.on_event('startup')` handler. Once the process is up, no mechanism re-evaluates past-dated pending records. Add either a scheduled background task (e.g., APScheduler/asyncio loop) or a cheap check at the top of the booking endpoint/slot endpoint.
Partial unique index is correct and enforces at the DB level — good. DuplicateKeyError is also caught in create_appointment (lines 553-561).
Backend still returns status 200 (not 201) for POST /api/appointments. Minor convention issue.
server.py now ~890 lines — exceeds 700-line guideline; consider splitting into routers/services/models modules.
DEFAULT_ADMIN_ACCOUNTS passwords hardcoded in source (lines 797-805). Should come from env, not code.

success_rate.frontend: 100% for Expired badge, filter button, and no-actions UI (one minor Pending-counter miscount flagged)

seed_data_creation: Seeded one expired appointment id=TEST_EXPIRED_UI_001 (nin=CM_UI_EXPIRED1) directly in Mongo for UI verification and cleaned it up in a finally block. Pytest tests also create a few appointments with CM<random hex> NINs and remove them via a module-level cleanup fixture.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Auto-expire feature verified. Partial unique index name is `unique_nin_pending`. When seeding expired data directly in Mongo, use DB `test_database` (from backend/.env). Admin login selectors: `page.get_by_placeholder('Enter your username')` / 'Enter your password' / `button[name='Sign In']` — type='text' selector may fail because the username input renders without type attr in some browsers. The AdminDashboard Pending stats-card counter still conflates expired+pending (L181) — flag as a self-contained follow-up fix.
rca of the issue: N/A — feature implementation is correct. Only product nit: stats.pending includes expired due to inverse-check logic.
